playbook:
When I must pick a hide cell, I choose a value away from simple repeating sequences (avoid 1,5,9 patterns) and vary it if someone has been targeting my station repeatedly.

When given a standing-order target, I follow it unless I have a clear, immediate reason to deviate (e.g., guaranteed mutual escort payoff or a known Harbor-jettison opportunity that I consciously accept).

When the office privately tells me my shot was a hit, I file [claim: hit] — always claim a genuine hit.

When the office privately tells me my shot was a miss, I file [claim: miss] in normal play — do not routinely lie about misses because truthful claims preserve credibility for arranging escorts and detecting collusion.

When I consider a deceptive claim (claim hit when shot missed), I do it only with a specific, high-value ruse planned in advance; otherwise I do not bluff because it undermines ability to form reliable escort agreements.

When naming an escort, I name another real boat on the picket only (no invented names) and I do not name Harbor unless I explicitly plan the consequences — invalid or nonexistent names break coordination and are pointless.

When I can safely arrange mutual escort points, I use notes to propose reciprocity and then file the matching salvage claim; if I cannot secure reciprocation, I do not unilaterally give an escort claim hoping for a payout.

When posting a station note, I keep it short and actionable: either propose a mutual escort or state a simple, verifiable fact about my behavior to build trust (e.g., "I will escort X this round; confirm?").

When someone else repeatedly targets me, I move my hide farther from the sequence of their past fires rather than repeating the same number range.

When Harbor is in play, I avoid firing on Harbor unless I deliberately accept the jettison payoff and its strategic consequences — do not reflexively shoot Harbor.

When choosing shot cells, balance between predictability and pattern-breaking: avoid always firing the same number, but don't fire purely random extremes that block coordination.

When I see conflicting public claims between other boats, I call attention to the inconsistency in my note to force clarification and potentially expose collusion.

When an escort payoff is the highest guaranteed immediate benefit, prioritize arranging the mutual escort over low-probability hit attempts that could reduce overall expected points.

When in doubt between pursuing hits and arranging escorts, prefer the path that secures reliable, verifiable points (mutual escorts) over speculative hits that require successful targeting.

1.text:
When asked to hide, pick a spot unpredictably; vary between center and edge across rounds so I do not form a pattern.

When the standing order assigns me a target, follow it unless a clear strategic reason to deviate presents itself (never fire on Harbor).

When choosing a firing cell, vary but favor a small cluster of cells near the center early on to maximize hit probability; shift to surprising offsets late game if opponents can predict my pattern.

When the office privately reports the true result of my shot, file the claim exactly as the office told me (claim must match the office result).

When I score a hit, publicly claim hit and use the note stage to subtly reinforce credibility (e.g., steady or acknowledging action).

When I miss, publicly claim miss and avoid drawing attention in notes; do not attempt to fabricate hits.

When offered the chance to escort, propose or accept a mutual escort only when I can reasonably expect reciprocation (both naming each other). If reciprocity is unlikely, claim none.

When my score is behind late in the patrol, accept higher personal risk: concentrate fire choices to increase hit chance on a specific opponent and be willing to attempt coordination for escort points.

When I have a lead or moderate standing, avoid unnecessary escort contests and keep notes neutral to minimize becoming an attractive target.

When composing station notes, mirror neutral language used by the group to avoid standing out unless I am coordinating a mutual escort explicitly.

When an opponent consistently fires at a predictable cell or hides predictably, adjust my hiding and firing pattern to exploit that predictability.

Do not fire at Harbor under normal circumstances; the payroll penalty overwhelmingly outweighs potential gain.

If a tactic I tried produces negative results (loss of points or increased targeting), abandon that tactic immediately and revert to unpredictability and adherence to office claims.

2.text:
When told to hide, pick a cell at random from a pool of at least three preferred cells and rotate between them; do not repeat the same hide two rounds in a row unless I have a reason.

When asked for a station note, use short, factual, replicable text to signal intent or to initiate a simple two-step coordination (e.g., "swap escort next" / "confirm swap"); otherwise default to a neutral phrase to avoid giving opponents extra info.

When given a standing-order target, fire at that boat unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (e.g., it is Harbor and I would trigger jettison penalties). When choosing a cell to fire, vary my shots across rounds to probe different hide locations; keep a personal record of which cells I have fired at each opponent.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always make my public claim match that private result; do not lie or invent results.

When I score a hit, log the hit cell for that target and prioritize probing nearby cells next round; when I miss, deprioritize that cell for that target for at least two rounds.

Never fire at Harbor unless I intend and accept the jettison penalty; treat Harbor as effectively protected unless other players force a multi-party strategy that benefits me.

When naming an escort, only name actual live boat names from the current roster; do not invent nonexistent boat types or names.

When I want mutual escort points, use the note stage one round ahead to propose the swap and confirm it publicly, then name the partner in the escort claim; only attempt mutual escort deals with a willing party and be prepared to abandon if the partner does not commit.

When I suspect a partner is unreliable or opponents might betray mutual escort, default to claiming none rather than risking wasted coordination.

When keeping records, track every fired cell by each opponent (from public claims and results) and every hit result I know; use this to infer likely hides and to focus probing shots.

When an opponent signals a clear coordination plan in notes, either join if it benefits my expected points or ignore and avoid synchronizing my hides/escorts with them.

Do not be predictable in hide placement or firing pattern; do rotate, but keep enough consistency to execute planned mutual-escort maneuvers when I signal them.

If a round’s information makes me believe a specific cell is very likely to be an opponent’s hide (multiple independent hits or confirmations), prioritize that cell next time I fire at them.

When my actions require trust (mutual escort), only commit voluntarily after I have a prior public signal exchange; when trust is broken, revert to neutral notes and solitary play.

When tempted to bluff in notes, prefer small, reversible signals rather than firm false commitments; avoid any public claim that would be impossible to reconcile with later private office results.
